data.narrative:
Pyka is a Series B autonomous drone company founded by Michael Norcia, Chuma Ogunwole, Kyle Moore, and Nathan White. The company has raised $40M to date. The broader Drones & Autonomous sector contains eight identifiable private peers including Elroy Air, Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, and Joby Aviation, with no public comparables available.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation technique given data constraints. Using total capital raised ($40M) as a proxy for implied Series A valuation, a 1.9x step-up multiplier—standard for Series B to subsequent-stage progression—yields an implied valuation of $76M. This method assumes typical venture expansion dynamics within the sector but relies on capital raised as a valuation proxy rather than direct financial metrics.

Peer-median triangulation is not applicable. While seven same-sector peers exist, the narrow filters of stage-matching, adjacent-stage proximity, and similar valuation tier yielded fewer than three datapoints. An all-sector median would introduce excessive noise. The analysis therefore rests on a single method, narrowing confidence.

The quantitative analysis supports a range of $65M (low) to $87M (high), with a median of $76M. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable Series B financials within the autonomous drone subset, reliance on capital-raised proxies rather than revenue or unit economics, and limited visibility into stage-progression multiples specific to frontier hardware sectors. Validation would benefit from additional portfolio company benchmarks or revenue-based approaches.
